creativity.reason: Level 0: the business description covers enterprise HR, finance, spend, planning and AI-agent software in detail, and shows no creating or enabling of creative work; 'creativity' and 'design' refer only to software engineering.

community.reason: Level 2: employee learning platforms plus a named Giving & Doing community investment program whose reach is not quantified beyond a per-team grant cap.

cross_cultural.reason: Level 3: 13 Employee Belonging Councils with a disclosed membership share of over a quarter of employees, supported by pay equity analysis, skills-first hiring and culturally responsive mental health support.

entrepreneurship.reason: Level 1: only serving emerging and medium-sized business customers and strategic corporate venture investing, with no specific program aimed at founders' or small businesses' barriers.

notes: Workday Community (customer knowledge-sharing portal), customer training, and Workday Success Plans 'on-demand education' were treated as customer support and marketing, which the trap rule excludes, and were not scored for Community. Higher education is a customer industry, not an education business. Workday Build, Flowise Agent Builder and Workday Data Cloud were announced but are planned for fiscal 2027, and they enable software and agent building rather than creative work. Workday Marketplace lists partner integrations for enterprise customers and was not treated as a small-business seller marketplace. Workday Ventures was classed as own_innovation rather than enabling because the filing frames it as strategic investment for the company's ecosystem and initiatives; this was a borderline call resolved to the lower level. Annual Code of Conduct compliance training (100% completion) was excluded as compliance training. Fertility and adoption benefits were not scored as inclusion practices because the filing does not frame them that way. The Item 7 excerpts contain no additional qualifying activities.
